MVP Scope\n\nThe MVP intentionally operates under strict constraints.\n\n### Structured Data\n\nSupported:\n\n* Multiple database servers (MSSQL, PostgreSQL)\n* One metadata definition file per database schema\n* One ingestion workflow for generating vector embeddings per database schema\n* Fine-grained control over which tables and columns are exposed per schema\n\nCurrent databases:\n```text\nsupplychain_pgsql \u2192 rzinn1gd (PostgreSQL on AWS RDS)\n\nlocal_mssql       \u2192 Baxflex   (MSSQL local docker \u2014 attendance, leave, exception requests, compliance)\n```\n\nThe goal is to validate:\n\n* Metadata generation from live databases\n* Schema understanding via vector embeddings\n* Text-to-SQL generation with correct dialect per platform\n* Query execution against live databases\n* Evidence extraction\n\n---\n\n### Unstructured Data\n\nSupported:\n\n\n* PDF and Word documents (via PyMuPDF extractor)\n* Excel files containing structured contract/invoice records (via openpyxl)\n\nExpected volume:\n```text\n\nPDF/Word documents : \u2264 50 files\nExcel contract rows: hundreds to thousands of rows (batched ingestion)\n```\n\nExtraction via:\n```text\n\nPDF/Word \u2192 PyMuPDF Extractor (can be extended to Azure Document Intelligence)\nExcel    \u2192 openpyxl row-by-row reader with header normalization\n```\n\nChunking strategy:\n```text\n\nPDF/Word \u2192 Hybrid \u2014 structure-aware page chunking + paragraph/sentence boundary splitting\nExcel    \u2192 Row-level chunking \u2014 each row becomes one or more chunks\n           Embeddable text = semantic fields (product_description, material_description,\n           scope_description) + structured natural language summary of key contract fields\n           (supplier, dates, amounts, renewal terms, applicable country etc.)\n```\n\nThe goal is to validate:\n\n* Document extraction via PyMuPDF\n\n\n* Hybrid semantic chunking for PDF/Word\n* Row-level chunking with enriched embed text for Excel contract data\n* Unified retrieval across both document types in a single Qdrant collection\n* Evidence extraction\n* Mixed-source synthesis\n\n---\n\n### Retrieval Modes\n\nThe system handles all three modes:\n\n```text\nSQL Only\n```\n\n> How many exception requests are currently pending approval?\n> Which employees have taken the most leave this year?\n> Show me the top 5 most non-compliant employees this month\n\n```text\nDocument Only\n```\n\n> What are the payment terms for the Armis security monitoring contract?\n> Which contracts have auto-renewal clauses with more than 60 days notice required?\n> What SAP cloud services does Baxter subscribe to and what are the annual costs?\n> Do we have any contracts for e-invoicing services in Europe?\n> What cybersecurity-related contracts does Baxter have?\n\n```text\n\nSQL + Document (Mixed Intent)\n```\n\n> How many employees were non-compliant this month, and do we have any active workforce\n>   management software contracts that could help track attendance better?\n> How many exception requests are pending right now, and what security monitoring contracts\n>   do we have in place like Armis or ReliaQuest?\n> How many employees are in fully remote roles, and do we have any collaboration or\n>   remote work tool contracts like Slack or Google Workspace?\n> How many audit log entries were recorded this month, and what are our active\n>   cybersecurity contracts covering monitoring and incident response?\n\n---\n\n## Agent Architecture\n\n### Planner Agent (`src/agents/planner/`)\nTop-level LangGraph orchestrator. Routes queries to DB and/or File agents.\n\n```text\nNodes:\n  plan_node              \u2192 LLM Call 1: decides which agents to invoke\n  rewrite_query_node     \u2192 LLM Call 2: decomposes query into focused sub-queries\n                           per qualified agent (fires for single and multi-agent paths)\n                           Falls back to original query if LLM call fails\n  execute_agents_node    \u2192 fans out all sub-queries concurrently across agent subgraphs\n                           via asyncio.gather; collects results as lists per agent type\n  synthesize_node        \u2192 LLM Call 3: lightweight assembly of pr     e-summarized agent\n                           responses into final coherent answer; attaches raw evidence\n                           for auditability post-LLM\n  graceful_response_node \u2192 handles unanswerable queries gracefully\n```\n\n### DB Agent (`src/agents/db/`)\nLangGraph graph for structured data retrieval and SQL execution.\n\n```text\nNodes:\n  retrieve_schema_node  \u2192 embed query, search baxter-db-metadata collection\n  filter_chunks_node    \u2192 LLM Call: filters retrieved chunks to relevant ones only\n  generate_sql_node     \u2192 LLM Call: generates SQL per platform (T-SQL / PostgreSQL)\n                          self-corrects on execution errors (max 3 retries)\n  validate_sql_node     \u2192 rule-based safety check, blocks DML statements\n  execute_sql_node      \u2192 executes validated SQL concurrently per database\n  db_synthesize_node    \u2192 LLM Call: interprets SQL results into focused summary\n                          short-circuits without LLM call if no data or errors\n```\n\n### File Agent (`src/agents/file/`)\nLangGraph graph for document retrieval and interpretation.\n\n```text\nNodes:\n  retrieve_documents_node \u2192 embed query, search baxter-documents collection\n  file_synthesize_node    \u2192 LLM Call: interprets retrieved chunks into focused summary\n                            short-circuits without LLM call if no chunks found\n```\n\n---\n\n## Response Model\n\nThe system is evidence-driven. Every response retains full evidence for explainability and auditability.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"answer\": \"...\",\n  \"confidence\": 0.91,\n  \"sources\": [\n    { \"type\": \"database\", \"name\": \"rzinn1gd\" },\n    { \"type\": \"document\", \"name\": \"proposal.pdf\" }\n  ],\n  \"evidence\": [\n    {\n      \"source_type\": \"database\",\n      \"source_name\": \"rzinn1gd\",\n      \"platform\": \"pgsql\",\n      \"sql_query\": \"SELECT ... FROM supplychain.inventory ORDER BY available_quantity DESC LIMIT 5\",\n      \"results\": [...]\n    },\n    {\n      \"source_type\": \"document\",\n      \"source_name\": \"proposal.pdf\",\n      \"page_number\": 1,\n      \"chunk_id\": \"proposal.pdf_page_1_chunk_1\",\n      \"text\": \"...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## LLM Usage\n\n| Node | LLM Call | Purpose |\n|------|----------|---------|\n| `plan_node` | Structured | Route query to correct agent(s) |\n| `rewrite_query_node` | Structured | Decompose query into focused sub-queries per agent |\n| `filter_chunks_node` | Structured | Filter irrelevant schema chunks |\n| `generate_sql_node` | Structured | Generate SQL per platform (with self-correction on retry) |\n| `db_synthesize_node` | Structured | Interpret SQL results into focused summary |\n| `file_synthesize_node` | Structured | Interpret document chunks into focused summary |\n| `synthesize_node` | Structured | Lightweight assembly of agent summaries into final answer |\n\n\n\nModel: `Claude Sonnet 4.6`\n\n---\n\n## Handling Broad Queries (\"The common 'Show Me All' problem in RAG\")\n\nA common user pattern in BI systems is open-ended bulk requests:\n> *\"Show me all contracts\"*, *\"Give me summaries of every document\"*, *\"List all inventory items\"*\n\nThese queries are fundamentally incompatible with precision retrieval \u2014 the system is designed\nas a focused question-answering assistant, not a data dump pipe. Baxter <settings.CHATBOT_NAME> handles this\nconsistently across both agent types:\n\n### DB Agent \u2014 Hard + Soft Row Caps\n```text\nFetch cap    \u2192 MAX_ROWS_PER_QUERY = 100   hard cap at DB driver level (cursor.fetchmany)\nDisplay cap  \u2192 MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS = 20      soft cap enforced in DB synthesis prompt\nFootnote     \u2192 \u26a0\ufe0f Showing 20 of 100 records. Results have been truncated \u2014\n               try a more specific query to narrow down the results.\n```\n\n### File Agent \u2014 Retrieval + Rerank Caps\n```text\nRetrieval cap \u2192 RETRIEVAL_TOP_K = 30     hard cap at Qdrant vector search level\nRerank cap    \u2192 RERANK_TOP_N = 5         precision filter via cross-encoder reranker\nFootnote      \u2192 \u26a0\ufe0f This summary is based on the most relevant documents retrieved\n               and may not represent all documents in the system.\n               Try a more specific query to narrow down and find a particular document.\n```\n\n### Why This Is The Right Approach\n\nThis mirrors how all major AI and BI systems handle bulk requests:\n- **Google** \u2014 \"About 2,000,000,000 results\" but shows page 1 only\n- **ChatGPT** \u2014 \"Here are some examples\" not \"here is everything\"\n- **PowerBI / Tableau** \u2014 \"Showing top 10 of 10,000 records\" by default\n\nAn AI assistant is a **precision instrument, not a data pipeline.**\nThe user's responsibility is to ask focused questions.\nThe system's responsibility is to answer them precisely with full transparency about scope.\nThe footnote is the honesty layer that makes responses trustworthy rather than misleading.\n\n## Embedding & Vector Store\n\n\n\n\n\n| Collection | Content | Source | Chunk Strategy |\n|------------|---------|--------|----------------|\n| `baxter-db-metadata` | DB schema metadata | Live databases | 1 per database + 1 per table |\n| `baxter-documents` | PDF/Word document chunks | Document files | Hybrid page/paragraph/sentence splitting |\n| `baxter-documents` | Contract/invoice records | Excel rows | Row-level \u2014 semantic fields + structured NL summary |\n\n\n> **Note:** PDF documents and Excel contract records share the same `baxter-documents` collection.\n> They coexist cleanly via `source_type` field in the payload (`\"document\"` vs `\"contract_record\"`).\n> At retrieval time the reranker surfaces the most relevant chunks regardless of source type.\n> The richer payload on contract records (supplier, dates, amounts, renewal terms etc.) is available\n> for the LLM to use in synthesis without affecting PDF chunks.\n\nEmbedding Model: `BAAI/llm-embedder` (768 dimensions) via self-hosted Ollama\nVector Store: `Qdrant` (running via Docker)\n\n---\n\n## Manual Ingestion (MVP)\n\nData ingestion is intentionally manual for the MVP. When we productionize, we will make this pipeline automated by enabling a UI to do all these housekeeping stuffs.\n\n### Step 1 \u2014 Generate DB Metadata\n```bash\n\nexport LOCAL_MSSQL_BAXFLEX_PWD=\"...\"\nexport SUPPLYCHAIN_PGSQL_RZINN1GD_PWD=\"...\"\npython scripts/generate_db_metadata.py\n```\n\n### Step 2 \u2014 Ingest DB Metadata into Qdrant\n```bash\npython scripts/ingest_db_metadata.py\n```\n\n\n### Step 3 \u2014 Ingest PDF/Word Documents into Qdrant\n```bash\n\n# place PDF or Word files in share/documents/\npython scripts/ingest_documents.py\n```\n\n### Step 4 \u2014 Ingest Excel Contract Records into Qdrant\n```bash\n# place Excel files in share/contracts/\npython scripts/ingest_contracts.py\n```\n\n> **Note:** Steps 3 and 4 both write into the `baxter-documents` Qdrant collection.\n> They can be run independently and in any order.\n\n---\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```text\nsrc/\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 agents/\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 db/           \u2190 DB agent LangGraph (retrieve \u2192 filter \u2192 generate SQL \u2192 validate \u2192 execute)\n\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 file/ proprietary format, NOT Oracle's built-in\n  TO_CHAR(date,'J') / TO_DATE(x,'J') Julian Day Number. Never use TO_CHAR(x,'J') or TO_DATE(x,'J')\n  for these columns \u2014 that is a different format entirely and will produce wrong results.\n  CRITICAL: In JDE, a Julian date column value of 0 (or NULL) conventionally means\n  \"date not set / not applicable\" \u2014 it is NOT a valid date. Passing 0 into the raw conversion\n  formula produces \"1900\" + day-of-year \"000\", which Oracle rejects with\n  ORA-01848 (day of year must be between 1 and 365/366). You MUST guard against 0/NULL\n  every time you convert a Julian column to a calendar date \u2014 whether in the SELECT list,\n  WHERE clause, or ORDER BY \u2014 using the NULL-safe formulas below.\n  Always use exactly these formulas instead:\n    \u2022 Julian column \u2192 calendar date (NULL-safe \u2014 use this any time a Julian column is\n      converted for display or comparison, including in SELECT lists):\n      CASE WHEN <col> IS NULL OR <col> = 0 THEN NULL\n           ELSE TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(1900 + TRUNC(<col>/1000)) || TO_CHAR(MOD(<col>,1000), 'FM000'), 'YYYYDDD')\n      END\n    \u2022 Calendar date or SYSDATE \u2192 Julian value (for WHERE clause comparisons):\n      (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM <date_expr>) - 1900) * 1000 + TO_CHAR(<date_expr>, 'DDD')\n    \u2022 Filter by a whole calendar year Y (e.g. year 2026):\n      TRUNC(<col>/1000) = Y - 1900   -- (also exclude <col> = 0 if the column can be unset)\n    \u2022 Filter \"today\":\n      <col> = (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM SYSDATE)-1900)*1000 + TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'DDD')\n    \u2022 Filter a date range (e.g. \"last 30 days\", or any range that may cross a year boundary):\n      convert the Julian column to a calendar date using the NULL-safe formula above, then\n      compare it against normal calendar dates \u2014 never compare raw Julian integers directly,\n      since e.g. 126001 (Jan 1, 2026) is numerically smaller than 125365 (Dec 31, 2025)\n      even though it is a later calendar date.\n    \u2022 When a Julian column appears only in the SELECT list for display (not the filter\n      condition itself), still ALWAYS wrap it in the NULL-safe CASE expression above \u2014\n      never assume every row has a valid non-zero Julian value, especially for optional\n      or not-yet-populated dates (e.g. a scheduled ship date before the shipment is\n      actually scheduled, or an actual-ship/invoice date before it happens).\n \n- Always qualify table names with the default_schema value from the schema context chunks \u2014 use exactly the value provided, do not invent or assume a schema/owner name\n- CRITICAL: Only use tables and columns that EXPLICITLY exist in the provided schema context chunks\n- CRITICAL: Never invent, assume or hallucinate column names \u2014 if a column does not appear in the schema chunks, do not use it\n- CRITICAL: If you cannot find the exact column name needed to answer the query in the schema context, use the closest available column that does exist \u2014 never fabricate one\n- CRITICAL: Before writing any column name in the SQL, verify it exists in the schema chunks provided\n- CRITICAL: Never invent, assume or hallucinate table names \u2014 if a table does not appear in the schema chunks, do not use it\n- Use JOINs where foreign key relationships are provided in the schema and only if necessary to answer the query\n- Keep queries focused \u2014 only SELECT what is needed to answer the question\n- CRITICAL: Never generate INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP or any data modification statements\n \n{error_context}\n \nUser Query:\n{query}\n \nRelevant Schema Context:\n{chunks}\n \nReturn a JSON object with:\n- queries: list of query objects, each containing:\n    - server_id: an identifier for the server/connection this query should be run against (can be same for multiple queries if they target the same database). This is used in downstream processing along with the database_name to determine the environment variable for the password value. E.g. if server_id is \"sales_db_server\" and database_name is \"sales_db\", downstream code will look for environment variable named SALES_DB_SERVER_SALES_DB_PWD to get the password for executing this query.\n    - MVP Scope\r\n\r\nThe MVP intentionally operates under strict constraints.\r\n\r\n### Structured Data\r\n\r\nSupported:\r\n\r\n* Multiple database servers (MSSQL, PostgreSQL)\r\n* One metadata definition file per database schema\r\n* One ingestion workflow for generating vector embeddings per database schema\r\n* Fine-grained control over which tables and columns are exposed per schema\r\n\r\nCurrent databases:\r\n```text\r\nsupplychain_pgsql \u2192 rzinn1gd (PostgreSQL on AWS RDS)\r\n\r\nlocal_mssql       \u2192 Baxflex   (MSSQL local docker \u2014 attendance, leave, exception requests, compliance)\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe goal is to validate:\r\n\r\n* Metadata generation from live databases\r\n* Schema understanding via vector embeddings\r\n* Text-to-SQL generation with correct dialect per platform\r\n* Query execution against live databases\r\n* Evidence extraction\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### Unstructured Data\r\n\r\nSupported:\r\n\r\n\r\n* PDF and Word documents (via PyMuPDF extractor)\r\n* Excel files containing structured contract/invoice records (via openpyxl)\r\n\r\nExpected volume:\r\n```text\r\n\r\nPDF/Word documents : \u2264 50 files\r\nExcel contract rows: hundreds to thousands of rows (batched ingestion)\r\n```\r\n\r\nExtraction via:\r\n```text\r\n\r\nPDF/Word \u2192 PyMuPDF Extractor (can be extended to Azure Document Intelligence)\r\nExcel    \u2192 openpyxl row-by-row reader with header normalization\r\n```\r\n\r\nChunking strategy:\r\n```text\r\n\r\nPDF/Word \u2192 Hybrid \u2014 structure-aware page chunking + paragraph/sentence boundary splitting\r\nExcel    \u2192 Row-level chunking \u2014 each row becomes one or more chunks\r\n           Embeddable text = semantic fields (product_description, material_description,\r\n           scope_description) + structured natural language summary of key contract fields\r\n           (supplier, dates, amounts, renewal terms, applicable country etc.)\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe goal is to validate:\r\n\r\n* Document extraction via PyMuPDF\r\n\r\n\r\n* Hybrid semantic chunking for PDF/Word\r\n* Row-level chunking with enriched embed text for Excel contract data\r\n* Unified retrieval across both document types in a single Qdrant collection\r\n* Evidence extraction\r\n* Mixed-source synthesis\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n### Retrieval Modes\r\n\r\nThe system handles all three modes:\r\n\r\n```text\r\nSQL Only\r\n```\r\n\r\n> How many exception requests are currently pending approval?\r\n> Which employees have taken the most leave this year?\r\n> Show me the top 5 most non-compliant employees this month\r\n\r\n```text\r\nDocument Only\r\n```\r\n\r\n> What are the payment terms for the Armis security monitoring contract?\r\n> Which contracts have auto-renewal clauses with more than 60 days notice required?\r\n> What SAP cloud services does Baxter subscribe to and what are the annual costs?\r\n> Do we have any contracts for e-invoicing services in Europe?\r\n> What cybersecurity-related contracts does Baxter have?\r\n\r\n```text\r\n\r\nSQL + Document (Mixed Intent)\r\n```\r\n\r\n> How many employees were non-compliant this month, and do we have any active workforce\r\n>   management software contracts that could help track attendance better?\r\n> How many exception requests are pending right now, and what security monitoring contracts\r\n>   do we have in place like Armis or ReliaQuest?\r\n> How many employees are in fully remote roles, and do we have any collaboration or\r\n>   remote work tool contracts like Slack or Google Workspace?\r\n> How many audit log entries were recorded this month, and what are our active\r\n>   cybersecurity contracts covering monitoring and incident response?\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Agent Architecture\r\n\r\n### Planner Agent (`src/agents/planner/`)\r\nTop-level LangGraph orchestrator. Routes queries to DB and/or File agents.\r\n\r\n```text\r\nNodes:\r\n  plan_node              \u2192 LLM Call 1: decides which agents to invoke\r\n  rewrite_query_node     \u2192 LLM Call 2: decomposes query into focused sub-queries\r\n                           per qualified agent (fires for single and multi-agent paths)\r\n                           Falls back to original query if LLM call fails\r\n  execute_agents_node    \u2192 fans out all sub-queries concurrently across agent subgraphs\r\n                           via asyncio.gather; collects results as lists per agent type\r\n  synthesize_node        \u2192 LLM Call 3: lightweight assembly of pr     e-summarized agent\r\n                           responses into final coherent answer; attaches raw evidence\r\n                           for auditability post-LLM\r\n  graceful_response_node \u2192 handles unanswerable queries gracefully\r\n```\r\n\r\n### DB Agent (`src/agents/db/`)\r\nLangGraph graph for structured data retrieval and SQL execution.\r\n\r\n```text\r\nNodes:\r\n  retrieve_schema_node  \u2192 embed query, search baxter-db-metadata collection\r\n  filter_chunks_node    \u2192 LLM Call: filters retrieved chunks to relevant ones only\r\n  generate_sql_node     \u2192 LLM Call: generates SQL per platform (T-SQL / PostgreSQL)\r\n                          self-corrects on execution errors (max 3 retries)\r\n  validate_sql_node     \u2192 rule-based safety check, blocks DML statements\r\n  execute_sql_node      \u2192 executes validated SQL concurrently per database\r\n  db_synthesize_node    \u2192 LLM Call: interprets SQL results into focused summary\r\n                          short-circuits without LLM call if no data or errors\r\n```\r\n\r\n### File Agent (`src/agents/file/`)\r\nLangGraph graph for document retrieval and interpretation.\r\n\r\n```text\r\nNodes:\r\n  retrieve_documents_node \u2192 embed query, search baxter-documents collection\r\n  file_synthesize_node    \u2192 LLM Call: interprets retrieved chunks into focused summary\r\n                            short-circuits without LLM call if no chunks found\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Response Model\r\n\r\nThe system is evidence-driven. Every response retains full evidence for explainability and auditability.\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"answer\": \"...\",\r\n  \"confidence\": 0.91,\r\n  \"sources\": [\r\n    { \"type\": \"database\", \"name\": \"rzinn1gd\" },\r\n    { \"type\": \"document\", \"name\": \"proposal.pdf\" }\r\n  ],\r\n  \"evidence\": [\r\n    {\r\n      \"source_type\": \"database\",\r\n      \"source_name\": \"rzinn1gd\",\r\n      \"platform\": \"pgsql\",\r\n      \"sql_query\": \"SELECT ... FROM supplychain.inventory ORDER BY available_quantity DESC LIMIT 5\",\r\n      \"results\": [...]\r\n    },\r\n    {\r\n      \"source_type\": \"document\",\r\n      \"source_name\": \"proposal.pdf\",\r\n      \"page_number\": 1,\r\n      \"chunk_id\": \"proposal.pdf_page_1_chunk_1\",\r\n      \"text\": \"...\"\r\n    }\r\n  ]\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## LLM Usage\r\n\r\n| Node | LLM Call | Purpose |\r\n|------|----------|---------|\r\n| `plan_node` | Structured | Route query to correct agent(s) |\r\n| `rewrite_query_node` | Structured | Decompose query into focused sub-queries per agent |\r\n| `filter_chunks_node` | Structured | Filter irrelevant schema chunks |\r\n| `generate_sql_node` | Structured | Generate SQL per platform (with self-correction on retry) |\r\n| `db_synthesize_node` | Structured | Interpret SQL results into focused summary |\r\n| `file_synthesize_node` | Structured | Interpret document chunks into focused summary |\r\n| `synthesize_node` | Structured | Lightweight assembly of agent summaries into final answer |\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\nModel: `Claude Sonnet 4.6`\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Handling Broad Queries (\"The common 'Show Me All' problem in RAG\")\r\n\r\nA common user pattern in BI systems is open-ended bulk requests:\r\n> *\"Show me all contracts\"*, *\"Give me summaries of every document\"*, *\"List all inventory items\"*\r\n\r\nThese queries are fundamentally incompatible with precision retrieval \u2014 the system is designed\r\nas a focused question-answering assistant, not a data dump pipe. Baxter <settings.CHATBOT_NAME> handles this\r\nconsistently across both agent types:\r\n\r\n### DB Agent \u2014 Hard + Soft Row Caps\r\n```text\r\nFetch cap    \u2192 MAX_ROWS_PER_QUERY = 100   hard cap at DB driver level (cursor.fetchmany)\r\nDisplay cap  \u2192 MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS = 20      soft cap enforced in DB synthesis prompt\r\nFootnote     \u2192 \u26a0\ufe0f Showing 20 of 100 records. Results have been truncated \u2014\r\n               try a more specific query to narrow down the results.\r\n```\r\n\r\n### File Agent \u2014 Retrieval + Rerank Caps\r\n```text\r\nRetrieval cap \u2192 RETRIEVAL_TOP_K = 30     hard cap at Qdrant vector search level\r\nRerank cap    \u2192 RERANK_TOP_N = 5         precision filter via cross-encoder reranker\r\nFootnote      \u2192 \u26a0\ufe0f This summary is based on the most relevant documents retrieved\r\n               and may not represent all documents in the system.\r\n               Try a more specific query to narrow down and find a particular document.\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Why This Is The Right Approach\r\n\r\nThis mirrors how all major AI and BI systems handle bulk requests:\r\n- **Google** \u2014 \"About 2,000,000,000 results\" but shows page 1 only\r\n- **ChatGPT** \u2014 \"Here are some examples\" not \"here is everything\"\r\n- **PowerBI / Tableau** \u2014 \"Showing top 10 of 10,000 records\" by default\r\n\r\nAn AI assistant is a **precision instrument, not a data pipeline.**\r\nThe user's responsibility is to ask focused questions.\r\nThe system's responsibility is to answer them precisely with full transparency about scope.\r\nThe footnote is the honesty layer that makes responses trustworthy rather than misleading.\r\n\r\n## Embedding & Vector Store\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n| Collection | Content | Source | Chunk Strategy |\r\n|------------|---------|--------|----------------|\r\n| `baxter-db-metadata` | DB schema metadata | Live databases | 1 per database + 1 per table |\r\n| `baxter-documents` | PDF/Word document chunks | Document files | Hybrid page/paragraph/sentence splitting |\r\n| `baxter-documents` | Contract/invoice records | Excel rows | Row-level \u2014 semantic fields + structured NL summary |\r\n\r\n\r\n> **Note:** PDF documents and Excel contract records share the same `baxter-documents` collection.\r\n> They coexist cleanly via `source_type` field in the payload (`\"document\"` vs `\"contract_record\"`).\r\n> At retrieval time the reranker surfaces the most relevant chunks regardless of source type.\r\n> The richer payload on contract records (supplier, dates, amounts, renewal terms etc.) is available\r\n> for the LLM to use in synthesis without affecting PDF chunks.\r\n\r\nEmbedding Model: `BAAI/llm-embedder` (768 dimensions) via self-hosted Ollama\r\nVector Store: `Qdrant` (running via Docker)\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Manual Ingestion (MVP)\r\n\r\nData ingestion is intentionally manual for the MVP. When we productionize, we will make this pipeline automated by enabling a UI to do all these housekeeping stuffs.\r\n\r\n### Step 1 \u2014 Generate DB Metadata\r\n```bash\r\n\r\nexport LOCAL_MSSQL_BAXFLEX_PWD=\"...\"\r\nexport SUPPLYCHAIN_PGSQL_RZINN1GD_PWD=\"...\"\r\npython scripts/generate_db_metadata.py\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Step 2 \u2014 Ingest DB Metadata into Qdrant\r\n```bash\r\npython scripts/ingest_db_metadata.py\r\n```\r\n\r\n\r\n### Step 3 \u2014 Ingest PDF/Word Documents into Qdrant\r\n```bash\r\n\r\n# place PDF or Word files in share/documents/\r\npython scripts/ingest_documents.py\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Step 4 \u2014 Ingest Excel Contract Records into Qdrant\r\n```bash\r\n# place Excel files in share/contracts/\r\npython scripts/ingest_contracts.py\r\n```\r\n\r\n> **Note:** Steps 3 and 4 both write into the `baxter-documents` Qdrant collection.\r\n> They can be run independently and in any order.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Project Structure\r\n\r\n```text\r\nsrc/\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 agents/\r\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 db/           \u2190 DB agent LangGraph (retrieve \u2192 filter \u2192 generate SQL \u2192 ingestion/\r\n\r\n\r\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 chunkers/\r\n\u2502   \u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 document_chunker.py    \u2190 Hybrid page/paragraph/sentence chunker for PDF/Word\r\n\u2502   \u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 excel_row_chunker.py   \u2190 Row-level chunker with structured NL summary for Excel\r\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 extractors/   \u2190 PyMuPDF extractor wrapper\r\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 db_metadata_ingestor.py\r\n\r\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 document_ingestor.py       \u2190 PDF/Word ingestion pipeline\r\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 excel_ingestor.py          \u2190 Excel contract/invoice ingestion pipeline\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 llm/              \u2190 LLM Engine + Extractor (Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Bedrock gateway)\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 metadata/\r\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 db/           \u2190 Generated schema JSON files + Pydantic models\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 rerank/           \u2190 RerankClient (cross-encoder reranker for file agent)\r\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 vector_store/     \u2190 Qdrant abstraction (upsert, retrieve, ensure_collection)\r\n\r\nscripts/\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 generate_db_metadata.py   \u2190 Step 1: generate metadata JSON from live DBs\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 ingest_db_metadata.py     \u2190 Step 2: embed + store schema metadata in Qdrant\r\n\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 ingest_documents.py       \u2190 Step 3: extract + embed + store PDF/Word docs in Qdrant\r\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 ingest_contracts.py       \u2190 Step 4: read + embed + store Excel contract rows in Qdrant\r\n\r\nshare/\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 config/\r\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 databases.yml          \u2190 Database connection config with schema/table/column filters\r\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 documents/                 \u2190 Drop PDF/Word metadata JSON files land here\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Infrastructure (Local Development)\r\n\r\n```yaml\r\nServices:\r\n  mssql:  localhost:1433  (SQL Server 2022 \u2014 local test database - just for local development)\r\n  qdrant: localhost:6333  (Vector DB \u2014 UI at http://localhost:6333/dashboard)\r\n```\r\n\r\nRun locally:\r\n```bash\r\ndocker-compose up -d\r\n```\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Architectural Principle\r\n\r\n```text\r\nAPI Layer          (FastAPI)\r\n    \u2193\r\nAgent Services     (process_query)\r\n    \u2193\r\nPlanner Graph      (LangGraph \u2014 plan \u2192 execute \u2192 synthesize)\r\n    \u2193\r\nDB Agent Graph     (LangGraph \u2014 retrieve \u2192 filter \u2192 generate \u2192 validate \u2192 execute)\r\nFile Agent Graph   (LangGraph \u2014 retrieve)\r\n    \u2193\r\nData Sources       (MSSQL, PostgreSQL, Qdrant, PyMuPDF, LLM Gateway)\r\n```\r\n\r\nEach layer communicates only with the layer directly beneath it.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Explicitly Out of Scope (MVP)\r\n\r\n\r\n* Automated ingestion (admin UI, scheduled sync, CDC)\r\n* NFRs like - Authentication / Authorization / RBAC\r\n* Multi-tenancy\r\n* Scale (multiple databases, hundreds of documents)\r\n* Tests\r\n* Observability (LangSmith, OpenTelemetry)\r\n* Conversation memory / follow-up questions\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Definition of Success\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n| Goal | Status
